haiku-low.q1: If reports.row_count (unfiltered, from replica) is 10,000 or less, the API streams a 200 text/csv download that the page saves. Above 10,000, it returns 202 queued and emails a download link when done.
haiku-low.q2: The API returns 200 with the existing export's id and status, and starts no new job, because the partial unique index rejects the second insert.
haiku-low.q3: The emailed link works for 24 hours. The stored file is removed by the bucket rule after 7 days, with no separate cleanup.
haiku-low.q4: Up to 3 attempts, numbered 1-3, with retries after 60 s and 300 s. After the last failure the row is set to failed, a failure email is sent, and the page shows 'Export failed. Click Download CSV to try again.'
haiku-low.q5: The replica. Every export path reads report rows from the replica only.
haiku-low.q6: In the report_exports row in the primary DB. The page polls GET /api/exports/{id} every 5 s while queued or running, and on load calls /api/reports/{report_id}/exports/latest.
haiku-low.q7: It reads 5,000-row batches from the replica and buffers CSV up to 8 MB, uploading each as a multipart part. Memory peaks at one batch plus one buffer, about 115 parts for 2M rows.
haiku-low.q8: On an exception the upload is aborted. A crash leaves an incomplete upload that is invisible and discarded after 24 h. The next attempt starts from row one with a new upload.
haiku-low.q9: Stored in the report_exports row as frozen filters and columns at insert time. The job payload carries only export_id, and the job loads filters and columns from that row.
haiku-low.q10: A partial unique index on (user_id, report_id) WHERE status IN ('queued','running') makes the second concurrent insert fail, which returns the existing export.
haiku-low.q11: The file must be completed with object_key set and a signed URL created. If the job reruns after finishing, it skips to mail if object_key is set, or does nothing if already succeeded.
haiku-low.q12: If the replica dies before the first byte it returns 503. If it dies mid-stream the connection drops. The page shows the export-failed message, saves nothing, and does not retry automatically.

sonnet.q1: Decided by unfiltered reports.row_count (from replica): 10,000 or less = sync download; more than 10,000 = background export. Sync: API returns 200 text/csv streamed, page saves it as a file; no job/record/storage. Background: 202 queued, user sees status labels and later gets an email with a download link.
sonnet.q2: The partial unique index on (user_id, report_id) for queued/running rejects the insert; the API returns 200 with the existing export's id and status and starts no new job.
sonnet.q3: The link (signed URL) works 24 hours (ttl 86400 s). The file is removed by the bucket's 7-day rule (lifecycle), 7 days after; no other cleanup.
sonnet.q4: 3 attempts (numbered 1-3; retries after 60 s and 300 s). After the 3rd failure, on_final_failure sets the row to failed (with error and finished_at), then sends a report_export_failed email (if that mail fails it is only logged). The page shows 'Export failed. Click Download CSV to try again.'
sonnet.q5: The replica only (all paths read report rows from the replica). The export record table is in the primary DB.
sonnet.q6: In the report_exports row (status column) in the primary DB. The page polls GET /api/exports/{export_id} every 5 s while queued/running until succeeded/failed. On page load it calls GET /api/reports/{report_id}/exports/latest to get the user's newest export, then polls that id; the page remembers nothing else.
sonnet.q7: It streams: reads 5,000 rows per batch from the replica (row_id > last ORDER BY row_id), CSV-encodes into a buffer, uploads an 8 MB part each time it fills, leftover as final part, then complete_multipart. Worst case memory is one batch plus one 8 MB buffer; ~115 parts (limit 10,000), well under 512 MB, a few minutes within the 30-minute timeout.
sonnet.q8: On an exception, abort_multipart is called then it re-raises. On a crash or 30-minute kill the upload is never completed so nothing is visible, and the bucket discards incomplete uploads after 24 h. The next attempt starts again from row one with a new multipart upload.
sonnet.q9: Stored (frozen) in the filters and columns fields of the report_exports row inserted at click time. The job payload contains only export_id, and the worker loads the row by that id to get them.
sonnet.q10: The partial unique index on report_exports (user_id, report_id) WHERE status IN ('queued','running') in the primary DB.
sonnet.q11: The file must be complete (complete_multipart done and object_key set on the row). Then the signed URL is made and the email sent, and only then is status set to succeeded plus finished_at. On a re-run: if status is succeeded or failed it just returns; if running with object_key already set it skips to the mail step (does not rewrite the file).
sonnet.q12: If the replica dies before the first byte: 503. If it dies mid-stream: the connection drops. The page shows the export-failed message and saves nothing; no automatic retry.
